gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, in ProjectorCentral's lab, the XGIMI MoGo 4 drops from 400–404 ISO lumens in Performance mode to 151–154 in the ECO mode its 2.5-hour battery claim depends on, so the battery-runtime advantage and the 'brighter than Capsule 3' claim come from different power modes.
standout_why: The cited iTechGuides MoGo 4 vs Capsule 3 page (2026-10-17) gives only maker specs: 450 ISO and 200 ANSI lumens, 2.5 h in Eco and a 20 ms rated lag. It reports RTINGS only as direction and says RTINGS' numbers are restricted. The RTINGS and TechRadar list pages didn't load. knowledgelib.io (uncited) gives one CNET figure for the Capsule 3 (about 123 lumens) and nothing measured for the MoGo 4 or MoGo 2 Pro. kiddofspeed.com and a2zcheck.com print only maker ratings. None of these pages has per-mode measured lumens, measured input lag or measured battery-mode brightness for the candidates.
decides: The finding confirms the MoGo 4 as the brighter pick when it's plugged in. ProjectorCentral measured about 400 lumens against 201 that Projector Reviews measured for the Capsule 3 in Bright mode, and 125–145 in its other modes. On battery the gap narrows: the MoGo 4 measured 151–154 lumens in ECO, which is the mode its 2.5-hour claim depends on. The Capsule 3 loses about 40% on battery (Projector Reviews), which by my arithmetic leaves roughly 75–120 lumens. Expert Reviews puts its runtime at 60–80 minutes at full brightness. The MoGo 2 Pro ($359 in ChatGPT's answer) measured 463 ANSI lumens on mains (Projector Reviews), above the MoGo 4's 400. That makes it the better value for brightness indoors. It is a 2023 test, with no measured lag. For gaming, the MoGo 4 measured 22.1 ms in Game Mode.
